extracted.intended_audience: writers submitting short science fiction and fantasy stories to Clarkesworld Magazine
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing and submitting short science fiction and fantasy stories to Clarkesworld Magazine, including length, format, rights, content preferences, and submission/process rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word limit
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories outside this range will not be accepted. The word limit is strict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay rate
rubrics_metrics.description: 10¢ per word for the first 5000 words, 8¢ for each word over 5000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment is calculated per word with a higher rate for the first 5000 words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted genres
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Science fiction need not be 'hard' SF, but rigor is appreciated. Fantasy can be folkloric, contemporary, surreal, etc. Horror can be supernatural or psychological, so long as it is frightening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and translations
rubrics_metrics.description: English (We accept stories from all over the world. Translations are welcome.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit English originals or translations; Clarkesworld accepts international submissions but publication language is English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights requested
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarkesworld claims first world electronic rights (text and audio), first print rights (author must be willing to sign copies), and non-exclusive anthology rights for their annual Clarkesworld anthology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unfamiliar with 'First Rights' the guidelines point to an explanation; authors should be prepared to sign for first print rights and grant non-exclusive anthology rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing quality / language importance
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories must be well-written. Language is important. There is no distinction between 'style' and 'substance' or 'story' and 'writing.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-quality prose and careful use of language are essential; weak language or sloppy craft will harm a submission regardless of concept.

rubrics_metrics.name: On-screen readability
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories should be convenient for on-screen reading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Very long paragraphs or typographical trickery may work against you. Prefer clear formatting suitable for reading on a screen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability for audio
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories should be suitable for audio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories should be equally effective, but not necessarily the same, in text and audio formats — keep audio performance in mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone/content expectations and use of extreme content
rubrics_metrics.description: No barriers as to levels of profanity, gore, or sexuality are stated, but high amounts of profanity, gore, and sexuality are generally used poorly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extreme content is allowed but must be used skillfully; gratuitous or poorly handled profanity/gore/sexuality will harm a story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hard sells / unlikely-to-accept content
rubrics_metrics.description: Though no particular setting, theme, or plot is anathema, the following are likely hard sells:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes (verbatim examples from guidelines): zombies or zombie-wannabes; sexy vampires, wanton werewolves, wicked witches, or demonic children; stories about rapists, murderers, child abusers, or cannibals; stories where the climax is dependent on the spilling of intestines; stories in which a milquetoast civilian government is depicted as the sole obstacle to either catching some depraved criminal or to an uncomplicated military victory; political takeover-by-party plots (Republicans, Democrats, Libertarians, Spartacist League, etc.); stories with archaic 'thou'/'thine'; talking cats or swords; stories where FTL travel or time travel is as easy as on TV/movies; stories that depend on vestigial belief in Judeo-Christian mythology to be frightening; stories about young kids finding ANYTHING (a body, alien craft, Excalibur, ANYTHING); stories about the stuff we all read in Scientific American three months ago; stories about your RPG character's adventures; 'funny' stories that depend on puns; stories where the protagonist is widely despised or admired simply because they are just so smart and/or strange; stories about an artsy-fartsy bohemia written by someone who hasn't experienced one; stories originally intended for someone's upcoming theme anthology; your trunk stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method and required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Do NOT email or mail submissions. Clarkesworld uses an online submissions system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the online form which asks for name, email address, cover letter, story title, word count, genre and story. Cover letter should contain your publishing history (if any) and any other relevant information (the guidelines joke that if you are an alien, mention it). All stories should be in standard manuscript format and can be submitted in either .RTF or .DOC format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous submissions policy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit the same story elsewhere while it is under consideration at Clarkesworld.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tracking, confirmation, and response time policy
rubrics_metrics.description: After submitting you receive a tracking number and an automated email confirmation containing this information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have not received the confirmation email within 24 hours, email them. The tracking number allows monitoring status on the website. Average response time is usually under two days, though they occasionally hold submissions longer. Do not send queries about pending submissions until after two weeks have passed; use your tracking number to check status prior to that.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-decision and query behavior rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't send revisions unless requested; don't submit another story for a period of seven days after receiving a rejection; don't re-submit stories that have been rejected; do not query for permission; don't argue with rejection letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If uncertain about any of these rules, follow the most conservative interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and limited disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Author's personal information (name, address, email, phone, or secret identity) will not be shared with anyone outside editorial staff except in listed situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions where personal info may be shared: if compelled by law; if threats are made against staff; if narrators require assistance with pronunciation (email only); if year's best editors request inclusion in their anthology (email only); or if the author has instructed them to do so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact for questions and technical issues
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have questions, concerns or technical issues, contact Neil via email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guidelines provide an email (neil@clarkesworldmagazine.com) for queries and technical support related to submissions and confirmations.
